style: Graham Potter's pragmatic 4-4-2 / 4-2-3-1 with structured defending and vertical, direct attacks. Wide forwards stretch high defensive lines to feed an elite strike pairing; the side leans on transition speed and the individual quality of its forwards rather than sustained possession.
recent_form: Dramatic turnaround under Potter, who took over in October 2025 with Sweden on one point from four qualifiers and steered them through, sealing a place via a 3-2 playoff win over Poland. Form trending up after a chaotic qualifying ride; in Group F with Tunisia, Netherlands and Japan.

key_players.name: Alexander Isak
key_players.note: Liverpool forward who leads the line with elite movement and finishing; one half of a fearsome strike pairing.

key_players.name: Viktor Gyokeres
key_players.note: Arsenal striker offering power, runs in behind and prolific scoring; forms an elite duo with Isak.

key_players.name: Anthony Elanga
key_players.note: Newcastle winger providing pace and width to stretch high defensive lines.

key_players.name: Victor Lindelof
key_players.note: Experienced centre-back organising the back line and bringing composure.

key_players.name: Emil Forsberg
key_players.note: Veteran playmaker supplying creativity and set-piece delivery behind the strikers.

historical_news: Graham Potter engineered one of the great recent qualifying turnarounds, rescuing Sweden from one point in four games to reach the finals.
Sweden sealed qualification with a 3-2 playoff win over Poland.
Dejan Kulusevski was left out of the squad after a year sidelined by knee surgery and setbacks.
Boasts one of the tournament's most fearsome strike pairings in Isak and Gyokeres.
Drawn into a tough Group F alongside the Netherlands, Japan and Tunisia.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Intrigue around a star-studded attack and Potter's rescue job, balanced by doubts over defensive solidity and a difficult group draw.
